title: Main Editor lags when Shader Editor has 'reload' dialog
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in 4.7.stable ### System information Godot v4.7.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 4 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1062) - AMD Ryzen 7 9700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.16 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description I've noticed for a while now that the entire Godot editor can become noticeably low-fps and feel like it's lagging when a Shader Editor has one (but more likely multiple, since one spawns for every opened .gdshader file or .gdshaderinc file) opened 'Reload Dialog', which asks whether to reload or resave the currently opened shader, after it has been changed externally. In my setup, the shader editor is a floating window on a second screen. Working in the script editor, or moving around in the 3D viewport show very clearly that the editor has low performance when these reload pop-ups exist. Moving in the 3D viewport feels like it has ~12 FPS, text in the script-editor appears delayed and moving the main editor around by dragging the entire window is extremely laggy. The in-editor FPS count does not show a drop in frames, which likely means the issue is on a higher level. Almost like it's in a 'unfocused' performance mode, despite being focused and receiving input. It seems the amount of reload popups worsens the effect. This happened both with `Editor Settings > Interface > Editor > Display > Update Continuously` on and off. I'm encountering this issue constantly due to a continuously syncing source control, and Godot incorrectly detecting changes to `.gdshader` files despite them being untouched. But that's a whole different issue, potentially to do with import files or uids. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the shader editor (in a separate floating window?) 2. Open a `.gdshader` file (preferably multiple) 3. Make external changes to one or more .gdshader files or preferably a `.gdshaderinc` file which is used in multiple opened shaders for convenience. (make changes in the text file, save a different shader under the same name or retrieve an update from source control) 4. When Godot realises the files need to be reloaded, it will create a 'Reload or Resave' dialog per unique file that is changed. 5. Ignore the dialog, and instead use the main editor window. Move around in a 3D viewport, write text in the script editor or move the engine window around 6. All editor behaviour will appear laggy and low-fps. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A. Behaviour does not get saved on disk, and only appears after external changes to a `.gdshader` file.
